God by him foretels the punishment of that abuse of power by the sword of war, and the desolations which the army of the Chaldeans should make upon them, ver. 5-11. III. 1.s: The Righteous Will Live by Faith
1.i: Habakkuk 1 and 2 are a conversation between a prophet and God, and give us the line the New Testament quotes three times.
1.p: Lord, we wait at our watch post. Help the righteous live by faith until the vision comes. Amen.
1.l: Write one question for God you have been carrying, and say it out loud as Habakkuk did.
q: God does not scold Habakkuk for asking questions. What questions do you think God welcomes?

3.o: Still the correspondence is kept up between God and his prophet. In the first chapter he spoke to God, then God to him, and then he to God again; in the second chapter God spoke wholly to him by the Spirit of prophecy; now, in this chapter, he speaks wholly to God by the Spirit of prayer, for he would not let the intercourse drop on his side, like a genuine son of Abraham, who "returned not to his place until God had left communing with him." Gen. xviii. 33.
3.i: Facing the loss of everything, the prophet Habakkuk chose to rejoice in the Lord, whose strength made his feet like a deer's on high places.
3.p: Lord, You are our strength when everything fails. Teach us to rejoice in You, whatever comes. Amen.
3.l: Name three things you are thankful for, even if today is a hard day, and say them out loud to God.
q: Habakkuk's yet I will rejoice came after he faced the worst. What helps you say yet in hard times?
